selection_protocol: Public-source audit sample using BNPB operational reporting plus Reuters national/context reporting, selected to test current adverse state, lagged context, response activity and verified local outcome lanes for August 2026 wildfire management.
known_gaps: Not an exhaustive census of all August wildfire incidents or all local BPBD reports.
Public reporting does not provide a complete live resource inventory or standardized containment-time denominator.
Local success cases differ in terrain, exposure and fire size from national/multi-region burden signals.

signals.summary: Public reporting citing Indonesia's forestry minister said nearly 95,000 hectares burned in July 2026, almost double the prior six-month burned area.
signals.direction_basis: Burned area accelerated sharply relative to the preceding six-month total, moving the national wildfire-loss state away from the desired low-burn condition.
signals.significance_basis: National-scale land loss increased sharply during peak dry-season risk.
notes: This report was published in August but describes a July condition period, so it is lagged risk/context rather than proof of the current August state.

signals.geography: Riau, South Sumatra, Jambi, West/Central/South Kalimantan
signals.summary: BNPB reported about 48,889.69 hectares burned across six priority provinces through 9 August and warned of unhealthy air quality and cross-border smoke risk.
signals.direction_basis: Large burned area plus unhealthy-air/cross-border-smoke risk represents persistent multi-region deterioration during the peak-risk period.
signals.significance_basis: Six priority provinces were simultaneously affected with environmental and population-health consequences.

signals.summary: Reuters reported that Indonesia's disaster agency was prioritizing Kalimantan after a recent rise in wildfire hotspots, with environmental and health concerns.
signals.direction_basis: A recent hotspot increase indicates worsening active-fire pressure in the current August operating period.
signals.significance_basis: The national disaster agency elevated Kalimantan response priority because of the hotspot rise and associated environmental/health risks.

signals.summary: BNPB documented simultaneous ground spraying and helicopter water bombing in Kubu Raya.
signals.significance_basis: Ground and aerial suppression were simultaneously active against difficult peat-fire conditions, making the response operationally important even though outcome improvement was not yet established.
notes: This is response activity, not proof that the fire condition improved. It must not enter the progress frontier by itself.

signals.summary: BNPB reported that a roughly 4.64-hectare fire affecting several villages in Paser had been extinguished.
signals.direction_basis: The incident state changed from active fire to extinguished/controlled, which is a direct movement toward the desired local safety condition.
notes: The outcome is a learning candidate; this record alone does not establish which intervention caused containment.

signals.geography: Klaten, Magetan, Jombang, Seram Bagian Timur
signals.summary: BNPB reported that the listed 8-10 August wildfire incidents were extinguished and caused no fatalities.
signals.direction_basis: Multiple individually active fire incidents transitioned to extinguished status without reported fatalities.
notes: Local success does not offset the wider national fire burden; it provides cases to study only after matching terrain, exposure, fire size and response context.
